agent_trace.summary: On brain MRI, ventricular abnormalities are assessed by comparing the size, shape, and symmetry of the lateral ventricles and third ventricle, as well as their relationship to the midline structures. Enlargement or distortion of the ventricles can reflect hydrocephalus, volume loss, obstruction, or congenital variation.

key_facts: The lateral ventricles should be symmetric or nearly symmetric in size and shape.
The third ventricle is normally a thin midline CSF space and should not be markedly widened.
Ventricular enlargement can be due to hydrocephalus or cerebral atrophy, while ventricular compression may occur with mass effect or edema.
Deviation of the ventricles or midline structures can suggest mass effect or asymmetric intracranial pathology.
Assessment should include surrounding sulci and white matter to help distinguish hydrocephalus from generalized atrophy.
